outcome: The exact conjecture (ch′(G) = χ′(G) for every graph) is still open as of 13 Oct 2026. The one post-2024 event that claims equality is Amir Jafari's single-author arXiv preprint 2608.22895 (v1 24 Aug 2026), which claims it, in its online form, for the complete graphs Kₚ₋₁ and K₂ₚ with p an odd prime; I could not verify it and found no engagement with it. Other post-2024 items are a talk-level improvement of the error term in the asymptotic bound (Molloy, 2024, no written version found), a 2024 journal publication of a 2020 local-Kahn preprint, and AI-credited counterexamples to neighbouring conjectures that do not bear on this one.
problem_asks: One universal equality, with one non-trivial half. (1) For every graph G (the frozen wording says 'every graph'; the literature states it for multigraphs in several places, Galvin, Kahn and Dhawan among them, so the scope is itself a question the judging pass will need to settle), the list chromatic index ch′(G), the least k such that G is k-edge-choosable, equals the chromatic index χ′(G), the least number of colours for a proper edge colouring. (2) The inequality χ′(G) ≤ ch′(G) is immediate (give every edge the same list of χ′ colours), so the content is the upper bound ch′(G) ≤ χ′(G): for every assignment of lists of size χ′(G) to the edges, a proper edge colouring from those lists exists. Nothing else is asked. Wikipedia's January 2024 wording is a single bullet with no sub-parts.

events.what_happened: Amir Jafari (single author) posted 'The List Edge-Coloring Conjecture for New Infinite Families', arXiv:2608.22895 [math.CO]. The paper claims the stronger online (edge-paintability) form of the conjecture, and hence the conjecture itself, for the complete graphs Kₚ₋₁ and K₂ₚ for every odd prime p. The method reduces the question to signed counts Sₙ over decompositions of Kₙ into perfect matchings (weighted by crossing parity), with congruences S_(p−1) ≡ (−2/p) mod p and S₂ₚ ≡ −p mod p². It also treats Kₙ with one perfect matching removed and K₂ₚ with some (not all) of a cyclic family of p disjoint perfect matchings. The reference list cites a companion manuscript, 'Prime symmetry behind list edge coloring' (2026), which I could not find.
events.revisions: v1 Mon 24 Aug 2026; v2 Wed 16 Sep 2026. The arXiv page gives no description of what changed between versions.
events.delivers: For the complete graphs Kₚ₋₁ and K₂ₚ (p an odd prime), claims χ′ = χ′ℓ = χ′P, where χ′P is the edge-paintability index, so that the conjecture holds for these graphs in its online form. Restricted to two infinite families of complete graphs; no statement for any other graph. Named members include K₆, K₁₀, K₁₂ and K₁₆ (from Kₚ₋₁) and K₆, K₁₀, K₁₄ and K₂₂ (from K₂ₚ). The variants with deleted perfect matchings are claimed as well, but I have not checked them.
events.remains: Every graph outside those families, which includes the general conjecture for graphs and for multigraphs. For example K₅₀ is outside this paper, outside Schauz's Kₚ₊₁ family (since 49 is not prime) and outside Häggkvist–Janssen's odd-order bound, because 49, 51 and 25 are all composite.
events.time_since_posted: About 7 weeks (50 days from v1 on 24 Aug 2026 to 13 Oct 2026). No review, blog post, comment or citing paper found. The search index is thin for 2026, so this is a weak negative.
events.directly_checkable: The congruences are checkable by machine for small cases: enumerate the decompositions of K₆ and K₁₀ into perfect matchings, compute the signed counts Sₙ, and check the congruences and the resulting online colourability for those graphs. I did not do this, and I did not find a computed table in the sources I could read.
events.doubts: (a) An unrefereed single-author preprint from an author with no other math.CO work found in searches; the author is not otherwise visible in the sources I could reach. (b) The companion manuscript that the paper's method rests on ('Prime symmetry behind list edge coloring') could not be found. (c) The paper states that the companion method 'yields no further coloring cases beyond the two exceptional translation configurations', so the families are the boundary of what the method gives, not a general argument. (d) I read the paper through a summarising fetch of the HTML v2, because the PDF returned compressed bytes. The theorem statements and reference list came from that summary, and I did not check the algebra. (e) The paper's small cases agree with the independently cited values: K₆ = 5 (Schauz et al. 2014) and K₁₀ = 9 (Rabern, unpublished). Agreement with these is a consistency check, not evidence that the proof is correct. (f) One search snippet, from an unidentified source, says no proof is known for K₁₆. Under the paper's family K₁₆ is K_(p−1) with p = 17, so the paper would cover it if correct. That snippet is unverified. None of these is a verdict; each is a signal for the judging pass.
events.direction: Cuts in favour of the conjecture: it asserts equality (and the stronger online equality) for the two complete-graph families. Nothing in the paper cuts against it.

events.what_happened: Alexey Gordeev, 'Proof of the List Coloring Conjecture for line perfect multigraphs', arXiv:1904.06662 [math.CO]. Claims that for a line-perfect multigraph the chromatic index equals the list chromatic index, a generalisation of Galvin's bipartite result. The abstract says the same result had already appeared in Peterson and Woodall (1999) by a similar but not identical method. No journal is listed on the arXiv page.
events.revisions: v1 14 Apr 2019; v2 27 Apr 2019; v3 5 Sep 2019 (last revised).
events.delivers: ch′ = χ′ for line-perfect multigraphs, as claimed. Restricted to a class of multigraphs (line graphs of which are perfect, in the paper's terms).
events.time_since_posted: About 6.5 years. No publication or engagement found beyond the author's own note about Peterson and Woodall.
events.doubts: The author says the same theorem was already published by Peterson and Woodall, so this is a priority question rather than a correctness one. The arXiv page does not say whether it was ever published.
events.direction: Cuts in favour (equality) for the class of line-perfect multigraphs.

events.what_happened: Joshua Harrelson and Jessica McDonald, 'List-Edge-Coloring Triangulations with Maximum Degree at most 5', arXiv:1909.01260. Abstract, verbatim: 'We prove that triangulations with maximum degree at most 5 satisfy the List-Edge-Coloring Conjecture.' A search index lists the journal as Australasian Journal of Combinatorics 88 (2024) 127–143. I could not read that PDF, so the journal entry is unconfirmed.
events.delivers: ch′ = χ′ for triangulations with maximum degree at most 5. Restricted to one class of graphs. The abstract does not say whether the graphs are required to be simple.
events.remains: All other graphs, including triangulations of larger maximum degree and all non-triangulated graphs.

checked_by.who: Australasian Journal of Combinatorics (journal of record, per a search-index listing)
checked_by.what_they_did: Published as vol. 88 (2024), pp. 127–143, according to the search index. Not confirmed from the PDF, which I could not read.

events.direction: Cuts in favour (equality) for triangulations of maximum degree at most 5.

events.what_happened: Marthe Bonamy, Michelle Delcourt, Richard Lang and Luke Postle, 'Edge-colouring graphs with local list sizes', arXiv:2007.14944. Main result, from the abstract: a local generalisation of Kahn's theorem. For a graph with large maximum degree Δ and minimum degree at least ln²⁵Δ, any list assignment with |L(e)| ≥ (1+o(1))·max{deg(u), deg(v)} for each edge e = uv admits an L-edge-colouring. The abstract cites Kahn (1996) for the asymptotic conjecture. The arXiv comment says 'Accepted to JCTB'; a search index gives JCTB 165 (2024) 68–96, which I did not open.
events.revisions: v1 29 Jul 2020; v2 8 Nov 2023 (current).
events.delivers: Asymptotic and local: for graphs with large Δ and δ ≥ ln²⁵Δ, lists of size (1+o(1))·max{deg(u), deg(v)} on each edge suffice. This is a statement about list sizes of order the maximum degree, not exact equality for any finite graph.
events.remains: Exact equality ch′ = χ′ for every graph; graphs with small Δ or small minimum degree; the o(1) term is not quantified.

checked_by.who: Journal of Combinatorial Theory B (accepted, per the arXiv comment)
checked_by.what_they_did: Accepted for publication. The arXiv comment says so; the 2024 publication was not opened.

events.direction: Cuts in favour, asymptotically and locally. It says nothing about exact equality.

events.what_happened: Michael Molloy gave talks on an improved bound for the List Colouring Conjecture. The UCSD combinatorics seminar was on 21 May 2024 (title 'An improved bound for the List Colouring Conjecture', from a search snippet; the abstract PDF returned unreadable bytes). The Toronto Metropolitan University colloquium 'Improved Bounds on the List Colouring Conjecture' was on 28 Nov 2024 (page opened). Stated result: the list chromatic index is at most D + D^(2/5)·poly(log D), improving Molloy–Reed's D + D^(1/2)·poly(log D), where D is the maximum degree. No preprint, arXiv number or journal was found.
events.revisions: No written version located. The first public mention is the May 2024 seminar abstract, but the write-up date is unknown, so the event is dated to the year.
events.delivers: ch′ ≤ D + D^(2/5)·poly(log D). This tightens the error term in the asymptotic bound relative to Δ. It is not equality, and it does not decide whether ch′ = χ′. The talk pages do not say whether the result is for simple graphs or multigraphs.
events.remains: Exact equality ch′ = χ′ for any graph; whether the error term can be removed altogether.
events.time_since_posted: About 17 months since the first talk (May 2024). No written argument has been located, so nobody can have engaged with it on paper.
events.doubts: The result is known only through talk announcements. The UCSD abstract spells Kahn as 'Khan', which looks like a typo. I did not see the argument, so I cannot say whether it is for simple graphs or multigraphs.
events.direction: Cuts in favour of the asymptotic statement only: it improves the error term but leaves the conjecture open.
sources: https://mathweb.ucsd.edu/~combosem/abstract-Molloy24_May.pdf (unreadable; date and title from search snippet)

events.what_happened: Simona Boyadzhiyska, Richard Lang, Allan Lo and Michael Molloy, 'Simultaneous edge-colourings', arXiv:2411.04071 (single version, 6 Nov 2024). A generalisation of Vizing's theorem in which k graphs on the same vertex set are edge-coloured simultaneously. Gives asymptotically optimal bounds for small k, and √k·Δ + o(Δ) colours in general. The abstract says 'Finally, our results extend to the list setting.'
events.revisions: v1 6 Nov 2024 only.
events.delivers: Asymptotic bounds on the number of colours for simultaneous edge colourings of k graphs, and list-setting extensions of these. These concern a different colouring problem, and the abstract gives no bound on ch′ of a single graph against χ′ of that graph.
events.remains: Everything the conjecture asks. The paper is not about ch′ = χ′ for a single graph.
events.direction: Neither way for this conjecture. It is a neighbouring result on simultaneous colouring.

events.what_happened: Parikshit Chalise, 'Sufficiency of Hall's Condition for Graphic List Coloring', arXiv:2609.01889 (1 Sep 2026, single version). Graphic list colouring: H is G-colourable if H has a proper vertex list colouring with L(v) = N_G(v). The paper characterises the graphs H for which Hall's condition (Hilton–Johnson, 1990) is sufficient for G-colourability, answering a question of Johnson, and gives complete results for forests, complete multipartite graphs and grid graphs. The paper is about vertex colouring. A search snippet had described graphic list colouring as the list version of edge colouring; the full text I read says it is vertex colouring and never mentions edge colouring.
events.revisions: v1 1 Sep 2026 only.
events.delivers: Results on vertex graphic list colouring under Hall-type conditions. Nothing on ch′ versus χ′.
events.direction: Neither way: it is off-topic for this conjecture.

systems.name: ChatGPT-5.6 Sol
systems.what_it_did: Per the author's declaration: identified counterexamples to the expectation that the restriction |V(H)∖V(F) | ≠ 4 could be dropped from Theorem 3.7, which led to Proposition 3.8; and constructed the graphs for the remaining 8-vertex cases in Figure 3. The paper says the tool did not prove Proposition 3.8 itself. The author says they reviewed, edited and verified the content and takes full responsibility.
systems.basis_quote: During the preparation of this work, the author used ChatGPT-5.6 Sol to resolve exceptional cases in Subsection 3.5.

events.what_happened: Jonathan A. Noel, 'The Partial List Colouring Conjecture is False', arXiv:2609.23291 (20 Sep 2026). Exhibits a 14-vertex graph with list chromatic number 3 and a 2-list assignment for which at most 9 vertices can be properly coloured from the lists. This disproves the Partial List Colouring Conjecture of Albertson, Grossman and Haas, which is a vertex-colouring conjecture. Abstract: 'This counterexample was discovered and fully verified by ChatGPT 6 Astra Ultra after some persistent prompting, but almost no mathematical input, from the author.'
events.revisions: v1 only.
events.delivers: Disproves a vertex-colouring conjecture. Says nothing about edge colouring or ch′ versus χ′.

checked_by.qualification: AI system, reported by the author as having verified the counterexample
checked_by.what_they_did: Reported by the author as having fully verified the counterexample.

events.directly_checkable: The 14-vertex graph and its 2-list assignment can be checked by hand or by a short program; I did not check them.
events.direction: Cuts against the neighbouring Partial List Colouring Conjecture. Neither way for this conjecture.

events.what_happened: Jonathan A. Noel, 'The List Total Colouring Conjecture is False', arXiv:2609.38417 (29 Sep 2026). Exhibits a cubic graph with total chromatic number 4 and list total chromatic number 5, disproving the list total colouring conjecture of Borodin, Kostochka and Woodall. Abstract: 'ChatGPT 6 Astra Ultra discovered the counterexample with little input from the author.' A MathWorld entry (search snippet only, not opened) gives 20 vertices and says the exposition was rewritten from ChatGPT-generated drafts.
events.revisions: v1 only.
events.delivers: Disproves the list total colouring conjecture. Total colouring colours vertices and edges together, so this is a neighbouring problem rather than list edge colouring.
events.direction: Neither way for this conjecture. It disproves a neighbouring conjecture.

systems.what_it_did: Per the author's abstract, discovered the counterexample with little input from the author.

events.what_happened: Guangming Jing, 'On Edge Coloring of Multigraphs', arXiv:2308.15588. Gives a polynomial-time algorithm that colours any multigraph with max{Δ+1, Γ} colours, confirming the Gupta–Goldberg–Andersen–Seymour conjecture algorithmically. The abstract says: 'The proofs of Theorems 3.2 and 3.3 were also verified by an AI-assisted audit using OpenAI's GPT-6 Pro model in ChatGPT; all resulting comments and revisions were independently evaluated by' (the text is cut off at that point on the page I read). The abstract page I read is the current version, v7 (13 Sep 2026), so the AI sentence is in a 2026 version; which version first carried it is not pinned.
events.delivers: An ordinary (not list) edge-colouring result for multigraphs: χ′ ≤ max{Δ+1, Γ} algorithmically. Says nothing about ch′.
events.doubts: The sole author describes an AI-assisted audit of two proofs, not an independent human reading of them. This is recorded for completeness; it concerns a different problem.
events.direction: Neither way for this conjecture. It is ordinary edge colouring.

events.what_happened: Fotis Iliopoulos and Alistair Sinclair, 'Efficiently list-edge coloring multigraphs asymptotically optimally', arXiv:1812.10309 (v1 26 Dec 2018; v3 7 Dec 2021). Polynomial-time algorithms that realise Kahn's non-constructive asymptotic results for list edge colouring of multigraphs, using a lopsided Lovász Local Lemma.
events.revisions: v1 26 Dec 2018; v2 unlisted; v3 7 Dec 2021.
events.delivers: Algorithmic versions of Kahn's asymptotic results. No new bound on ch′ against χ′ beyond Kahn's asymptotic claim, and the palette size is not stated in the abstract.
events.direction: Neither way for the exact conjecture. It makes Kahn's asymptotic results constructive.

events.what_happened: Ł. Kowalik and A. Socała, 'Tight Lower Bounds for List Edge Coloring', arXiv:1804.02537 (7 Apr 2018). Under ETH, list edge colouring of simple graphs has no algorithm running in time 2^(o(n²)), which matches the 2^m·n^O(1) upper bound.
events.delivers: A running-time lower bound. It says nothing about ch′ against χ′.
events.direction: Neither way. It is a complexity result on a neighbouring question.

events.what_happened: Joshua Harrelson, 'List-Edge-Coloring with Bounded Maximum Degree', arXiv:2207.03869 (v1 8 Jul 2022; v2 4 May 2023). Abstract: if mad(G) < m, where m depends on Δ, then ch′(G) ≤ Δ+1. The threshold m is about Δ/2 for Δ ≤ 20 and about Δ/4 + 5 for larger Δ.
events.revisions: v1 8 Jul 2022; v2 4 May 2023 (current).
events.delivers: ch′ ≤ Δ+1 for graphs whose maximum average degree is below a Δ-dependent threshold. This is a weaker, Vizing-type bound for a restricted class. It does not give ch′ = χ′.
events.remains: Equality for all graphs, and for graphs outside the mad threshold.
events.direction: Neither way for equality. It supports the weaker Vizing form for sparse graphs.

events.what_happened: Abhishek Dhawan, 'Multigraph edge-coloring with local list sizes', arXiv:2307.12094 (v1 22 Jul 2023; v2 3 Aug 2023; v3 15 Jan 2025). Gives sufficient conditions on a local function f for local list edge colourings of multigraphs. Corollaries are local analogues of Vizing's and Shannon's theorems, recovering a result of Conley, Grebík and Pikhurko. The abstract does not mention the list edge colouring conjecture.
events.revisions: v1 22 Jul 2023; v2 3 Aug 2023; v3 15 Jan 2025 (current).
events.delivers: Local analogues of Vizing's and Shannon's theorems for multigraphs. These are colour-count bounds in a local setting, not ch′ = χ′.
events.doubts: A search snippet said the paper builds on the list edge colouring conjecture; the abstract I read does not say so. I have treated it as neighbouring.
events.direction: Neither way for equality. It is a local, Vizing-type result for multigraphs.

events.what_happened: Uwe Schauz, 'Orientations of 1-Factorizations and the List Chromatic Index of Small Graphs', arXiv:1705.00484 (1 May 2017; single version as listed). Uses a corollary of the Quantitative Combinatorial Nullstellensatz together with the sign of 1-factorizations. The abstract says the author 'attempt[s] to prove the List Edge Coloring Conjecture for all graphs with up to 10 vertices' and that this leaves 'some exceptional cases' that the abstract does not name. The reference list of Jafari (2026) cites a 2018 journal version, Schauz, 'Computing the list chromatic index of graphs', J. Discrete Algorithms 52–53, which I did not open.
events.revisions: v1 1 May 2017 only, as listed.
events.delivers: An attempt at ch′ = χ′ for all graphs on at most 10 vertices, with unnamed exceptions. As a finite computation on a universal claim, it checks instances and does not reach the general statement.
events.remains: The unnamed exceptional cases, and every graph on 11 or more vertices.
events.directly_checkable: The computation is machine-based and the claimed results for small graphs can be checked by computer. I did not run it.
events.doubts: The abstract does not name the exceptional cases, so I cannot say which small graphs are settled. The 2018 journal version may differ from the arXiv abstract.
events.direction: In favour for the graphs covered. It settles no infinite class.

events.what_happened: Uwe Schauz, 'Proof of the List Edge Coloring Conjecture for Complete Graphs of Prime Degree', The Electronic Journal of Combinatorics 21(3), article P3.43 (published 18 Sep 2014; DOI 10.37236/4084). Proves ch′(Kₚ₊₁) = ch′P(Kₚ₊₁) = p for every odd prime p, using the Quantitative Combinatorial Nullstellensatz, the Paintability Nullstellensatz and a group action on symmetric Latin squares. Also gives a partial proof of a version of the Alon–Tarsi conjecture on even and odd Latin squares. The abstract says the result confirms the conjecture for complete graphs on fewer than 10 vertices and gives arbitrarily large class-1 complete graphs.
events.revisions: EJC publication 18 Sep 2014. I did not check for an earlier preprint, so the first public written argument may be earlier than the journal date.
events.delivers: ch′ = χ′ for Kₚ₊₁ with p an odd prime, that is, even-order complete graphs K₄, K₆, K₈, K₁₂, K₁₄, K₁₈ and so on.
events.remains: Every graph not of the form Kₚ₊₁ with p an odd prime. For example K₁₀ and K₁₆ are not in this family; Jafari (2026) covers K₁₀ and K₁₆ through a different family.

checked_by.who: The Electronic Journal of Combinatorics (journal of record)

events.direction: In favour (equality) for the complete graphs Kₚ₊₁, p an odd prime.

events.what_happened: Uwe Schauz, David Cariolaro, Gianfranco Cariolaro and Xu Sun, 'The list-chromatic index of K₆', Discrete Mathematics 322 (2014) 15–18, published 6 May 2014 (per a search-index listing, not opened). Shows ch′(K₆) = 5 = χ′(K₆), using computer algebra and the Combinatorial Nullstellensatz. The abstract is not in the sources I read.
events.delivers: ch′(K₆) = 5 = χ′(K₆). A single graph, which is also covered by the Kₚ₊₁ family with p = 5.

checked_by.who: Discrete Mathematics (journal of record, per a search-index listing)

events.directly_checkable: K₆ is small enough to check by computer.
events.direction: In favour (equality) for K₆ only.

events.what_happened: R. Häggkvist and J. C. M. Janssen, 'New bounds on the list-chromatic index of the complete graph and other simple graphs', Combinatorics, Probability and Computing 6 (1997) 295–313. Per secondary sources (search snippets, not opened): ch′(Kₙ) ≤ n for every n. This settles the conjecture for complete graphs of odd order, where χ′(Kₙ) = n. One search snippet also attributes a general bound of χ′ + Õ(χ′^(2/3)) to a refinement by these authors, which I could not verify.
events.revisions: I did not check for an earlier preprint.
events.delivers: ch′(Kₙ) ≤ n. Together with χ′(Kₙ) = n for odd n, equality for complete graphs of odd order.
events.remains: Complete graphs of even order, where χ′(Kₙ) = n−1 and the upper bound n is one too high; and all non-complete graphs.

checked_by.who: Combinatorics, Probability and Computing (journal of record)
checked_by.what_they_did: Published vol. 6 (1997), pp. 295–313, as listed in secondary citations. Not opened.
checked_by.where: Reference listed in Jafari (2026) and in the search snippets; no URL opened

events.doubts: Known to me only through secondary sources; the exact statements are unverified.
events.direction: In favour (equality) for complete graphs of odd order.
sources: https://arxiv.org/html/2608.22895v2 (cites it; the 1997 paper not opened)

events.what_happened: Jeff Kahn, 'Asymptotics of the list-chromatic index for multigraphs', Random Structures & Algorithms 17(2) (2000) 117–156. Per the journal listing in a search index and per Iliopoulos–Sinclair (opened): ch′(G) ~ χ′*(G) as ch′(G) → ∞ for multigraphs, where χ′* is the fractional chromatic index, so ch′(G) ≤ (1+o(1))χ′(G) in that regime. The proof samples hard-core distributions on matchings. A preprint is on Kahn's Rutgers page (LMULTI.pdf), which I could not read.
events.revisions: Journal year is 2000. The preprint date is not established.
events.delivers: Asymptotic: for multigraphs, ch′ is asymptotically equal to the fractional chromatic index, and hence to χ′, as the list index grows. The error term is o(1) and is not quantified.
events.remains: Exact equality for every multigraph; the asymptotic error term.
events.direction: In favour, asymptotically, for multigraphs.

events.what_happened: Jeff Kahn, 'Asymptotically good list-colorings', Journal of Combinatorial Theory A (1996). Cited by Bonamy et al. (opened) as the paper in which 'Kahn proved that the List Colouring Conjecture holds asymptotically'. The 1996 paper itself was not located or opened. A search snippet describes it as ch′(G) ≤ (1+o(1))χ′(G) for simple graphs, which is unverified.
events.delivers: Asymptotic: the list chromatic index is (1+o(1)) times the chromatic index, for the class covered (simple graphs per the snippet, unverified).
events.doubts: Scope (simple versus multigraphs) is not verified from the 1996 paper itself.
events.direction: In favour, asymptotically.

events.what_happened: Michael Molloy and Bruce Reed, 'The asymptotics of edge colouring multigraphs', a chapter in Graph Colouring and the Probabilistic Method (Springer, 2002 per a search listing; not opened). The Toronto talk page (opened) states the bound as ch′ ≤ D + D^(1/2)·poly(log D). The chapter's precise statement is not verified.
events.revisions: The first public written argument may be earlier than the 2002 book chapter.
events.delivers: Asymptotic: ch′ ≤ D + D^(1/2)·poly(log D). This tightens Kahn's o(D) error term for list edge colouring.
events.remains: Exact equality; the D^(1/2) error term (improved to D^(2/5) by Molloy, 2024, as a talk).
events.direction: In favour, asymptotically.

events.what_happened: Borodin, Kostochka and Woodall, 'List edge and list total colourings of multigraphs', Journal of Combinatorial Theory B 71 (1997) 184–204. Per a search snippet (not opened): for bipartite multigraphs with edge list sizes f(e) = max{d(u), d(w)}, the graph is edge-f-choosable, a local version of Galvin's theorem. For non-bipartite multigraphs, lists of size ⌊3Δ/2⌋ suffice.
events.delivers: A local, nonuniform-list version of Galvin's bipartite result, and a weaker palette bound (⌊3Δ/2⌋) for non-bipartite multigraphs. Neither is ch′ = χ′ for non-bipartite graphs.
events.doubts: Known only from a search snippet and a secondary citation; the exact theorem statements are not verified.
events.direction: In favour for bipartite multigraphs (a stronger, local form). Weaker for non-bipartite.

events.what_happened: Fred Galvin, 'The list chromatic index of a bipartite multigraph', Journal of Combinatorial Theory B 63(1) (1995) 153–158 (DOI 10.1006/jctb.1995.1011 per a search snippet). Proves ch′(G) = χ′(G) for every bipartite multigraph G, and hence ch′(G) = Δ(G) by König's theorem. Taking G = Kₙ,ₙ gives the Dinitz theorem on partial Latin squares. The Dinitz Wikipedia page (opened) says Galvin proved it in 1994; its citation is the 1995 journal paper.
events.revisions: Journal publication 1995. The Dinitz page dates the proof to 1994, and I did not find the preprint, so the year of first public written argument is 1994 or 1995.
events.delivers: ch′ = χ′ for every bipartite multigraph, which is the bipartite case of the conjecture for multigraphs.

checked_by.who: Journal of Combinatorial Theory B (journal of record)
checked_by.where: https://doi.org/10.1006/jctb.1995.1011 (DOI from a search snippet, not opened)

events.direction: In favour (equality) for the bipartite class.

events.what_happened: Mark N. Ellingham and Luis Goddyn, 'List edge colourings of some 1-factorable multigraphs', Combinatorica 16 (1996) 343–352 (DOI 10.1007/BF01261320 per a bibliographic snippet, not opened). Uses the Alon–Tarsi method to verify the conjecture for certain families of 1-factorable multigraphs, including 1-factorable planar graphs. A 2010 SFU thesis summary, seen in a search snippet, says that for planar cubic graphs only partial results are known.

summary: No source I found resolves the conjecture for all graphs or multigraphs as of 13 Oct 2026. The only post-January-2024 event that claims equality for a class of graphs is Amir Jafari's single-author preprint arXiv:2608.22895 (v1 24 Aug 2026, v2 16 Sep 2026). It claims the online (edge-paintability) form of the conjecture, and hence the conjecture, for the complete graphs Kₚ₋₁ and K₂ₚ with p an odd prime, via congruences for signed decomposition counts. I read the arXiv abstract page (v1 and v2 dates) and the HTML v2 through a summarising fetch, since the PDF returned compressed bytes. I did not check the algebra. The paper's result is a restriction to two infinite families of complete graphs. Measured against the frozen statement's universal wording, it settles those instances and nothing else, which is the judging pass's call to make. The paper cites a companion manuscript, 'Prime symmetry behind list edge coloring' (2026), which I could not find. Nobody has engaged with the paper publicly in the sources I could reach (no review, comment, blog or citing paper), but the 2026 search index is thin, so that is a weak negative. Other post-2024 events: Molloy's talk-level improvement of the asymptotic error term (D + D^(2/5)·poly(log D), 2024; no written version located, and the talks do not say whether the result is for simple graphs or multigraphs); Boyadzhiyska, Lang, Lo and Molloy's simultaneous edge-colouring paper (Nov 2024; neighbouring, not about ch′ versus χ′ for one graph); the 2024 JCTB publication of Bonamy, Delcourt, Lang and Postle's local Kahn theorem (preprint 2020). Earlier results, all recorded as separate events: Galvin's bipartite multigraph theorem (1994/95); Häggkvist and Janssen's bound for complete graphs (ch′(Kₙ) ≤ n, so equality for odd order, 1997); Kahn's asymptotic results (1996 for simple graphs, per a snippet and Bonamy et al.; 2000 for multigraphs); Schauz's Kₚ₊₁ theorem (EJC 2014) and his K₆ paper (2014), plus his 2017 arXiv attempt at all graphs of at most 10 vertices, which names no exceptions; Ellingham–Goddyn (1996) on 1-factorable multigraphs; Peterson–Woodall (1999) and Gordeev (2019) on line-perfect multigraphs; Harrelson–McDonald (arXiv 2019, journal 2024 per index) on triangulations of maximum degree 5; and weaker Vizing-type results for Δ ≤ 4 (1976, 1999) and for sparse graphs (Harrelson 2022). Rabern's K₁₀ value (2014) is known only from Jafari's citation. A close call on scope: the frozen statement says 'every graph', but the literature states the conjecture for multigraphs in several places (Galvin, Kahn, Dhawan, Iliopoulos–Sinclair), and results for simple graphs alone (Jafari's complete graphs, Harrelson–McDonald's triangulations) do not decide the multigraph version. A second close call: whether two infinite families of complete graphs count for anything depends on how the judging pass reads a family-of-instances result against a universal claim. The complete-graph families in this area currently cover K₁₆ (Jafari, via K_(p−1) with p = 17) but not K₅₀, which none of Jafari, Schauz's Kₚ₊₁ family nor Häggkvist–Janssen's odd-order bound reaches. AI involvement: no source I read names an AI system in any work on this conjecture. Searches for AlphaEvolve, GPT, Claude, Gemini, AI disclosures, the Breakthrough Tracker and Erdős problems found nothing on list edge colouring. The AI-credited records I found are on neighbouring problems and are recorded as discarded events: Chalise (arXiv 2609.01889; vertex graphic list colouring; author declares ChatGPT-5.6 Sol resolved exceptional cases and built 8-vertex graphs; the paper is vertex colouring, and a search snippet had wrongly called it edge colouring); Noel (arXiv 2609.23291; Partial List Colouring Conjecture; abstract credits ChatGPT 6 Astra Ultra with discovering and fully verifying a 14-vertex counterexample); Noel (arXiv 2609.38417; list total colouring; abstract credits ChatGPT 6 Astra Ultra with discovering the counterexample); and Jing (arXiv 2308.15588; ordinary multigraph edge colouring; abstract credits OpenAI's GPT-6 Pro with an AI-assisted audit of two proofs, which is checking, not load-bearing). Also seen but not opened and not on this problem: arXiv 2607.17421 (strong edge colouring; an unnamed agentic system used for Lean and sweeps; search snippet only). Lean/Coq: searches found no formalisation of the list edge colouring conjecture, the Dinitz theorem or Galvin's proof. Machine-checked status is therefore null throughout, as far as I could see.
competing_reading: Read as progress: Jafari's paper would be the first new infinite families of complete graphs covered by an equality result since Schauz's Kₚ₊₁ family (2014). It reaches K₁₆, K₂₂ and K₂₆, which that family does not, and its stronger online claim is more than the conjecture needs. Read as nothing settled: it is an unrefereed single-author preprint, the companion method is said by the paper itself to yield no cases beyond the two exceptional configurations, nobody has engaged with it in the seven weeks since posting, and a restriction to two infinite families of complete graphs leaves the universal claim about all graphs untouched. Read this way the record should count the event as a case, not a resolution. A further reading turns on scope: the frozen statement says 'every graph', while the literature usually means multigraphs. On the multigraph reading, Jafari's result is one class of simple graphs and settles nothing about multigraphs, so the judging pass may decide the question on either reading.
what_would_settle_it: (1) A referee report, a journal acceptance or an expert verification of arXiv:2608.22895, in particular the Glynn-coefficient and Pfaffian step for Kₚ₋₁ and the signed Burnside and starter-sum argument for K₂ₚ, and a check of the online (paintability) claim. (2) An independent computation of the signed counts Sₙ for n = 6 and n = 10, and of the online colourability of K₆ and K₁₀, against the paper's congruences. (3) The companion manuscript 'Prime symmetry behind list edge coloring', or any citing or responding paper. (4) A statement of whether the frozen 'every graph' is meant to include multigraphs, which the judging pass must settle. (5) For Molloy's D + D^(2/5)·poly(log D) bound: the written argument, and whether it holds for simple graphs or multigraphs. (6) For the older results, the primary papers (Galvin 1995, Häggkvist–Janssen 1997, Kahn 1996 and 2000, Schauz 2014 and 2017/2018, Ellingham–Goddyn 1996, Peterson–Woodall 1999, Juvan–Mohar–Škrekovski 1999), which I did not open, so their statements are as secondary sources report them.

event.what_happened: Amir Jafari (single author) posted 'The List Edge-Coloring Conjecture for New Infinite Families', arXiv:2608.22895 [math.CO]. The paper claims the stronger online (edge-paintability) form of the conjecture, and hence the conjecture itself, for the complete graphs Kₚ₋₁ and K₂ₚ for every odd prime p. The method reduces the question to signed counts Sₙ over decompositions of Kₙ into perfect matchings (weighted by crossing parity), with congruences S_(p−1) ≡ (−2/p) mod p and S₂ₚ ≡ −p mod p². It also treats Kₙ with one perfect matching removed and K₂ₚ with some (not all) of a cyclic family of p disjoint perfect matchings. The reference list cites a companion manuscript, 'Prime symmetry behind list edge coloring' (2026), which I could not find.
event.revisions: v1 Mon 24 Aug 2026; v2 Wed 16 Sep 2026. The arXiv page gives no description of what changed between versions.
event.delivers: For the complete graphs Kₚ₋₁ and K₂ₚ (p an odd prime), claims χ′ = χ′ℓ = χ′P, where χ′P is the edge-paintability index, so that the conjecture holds for these graphs in its online form. Restricted to two infinite families of complete graphs; no statement for any other graph. Named members include K₆, K₁₀, K₁₂ and K₁₆ (from Kₚ₋₁) and K₆, K₁₀, K₁₄ and K₂₂ (from K₂ₚ). The variants with deleted perfect matchings are claimed as well, but I have not checked them.
event.remains: Every graph outside those families, which includes the general conjecture for graphs and for multigraphs. For example K₅₀ is outside this paper, outside Schauz's Kₚ₊₁ family (since 49 is not prime) and outside Häggkvist–Janssen's odd-order bound, because 49, 51 and 25 are all composite.
event.time_since_posted: About 7 weeks (50 days from v1 on 24 Aug 2026 to 13 Oct 2026). No review, blog post, comment or citing paper found. The search index is thin for 2026, so this is a weak negative.
event.directly_checkable: The congruences are checkable by machine for small cases: enumerate the decompositions of K₆ and K₁₀ into perfect matchings, compute the signed counts Sₙ, and check the congruences and the resulting online colourability for those graphs. I did not do this, and I did not find a computed table in the sources I could read.
event.doubts: (a) An unrefereed single-author preprint from an author with no other math.CO work found in searches; the author is not otherwise visible in the sources I could reach. (b) The companion manuscript that the paper's method rests on ('Prime symmetry behind list edge coloring') could not be found. (c) The paper states that the companion method 'yields no further coloring cases beyond the two exceptional translation configurations', so the families are the boundary of what the method gives, not a general argument. (d) I read the paper through a summarising fetch of the HTML v2, because the PDF returned compressed bytes. The theorem statements and reference list came from that summary, and I did not check the algebra. (e) The paper's small cases agree with the independently cited values: K₆ = 5 (Schauz et al. 2014) and K₁₀ = 9 (Rabern, unpublished). Agreement with these is a consistency check, not evidence that the proof is correct. (f) One search snippet, from an unidentified source, says no proof is known for K₁₆. Under the paper's family K₁₆ is K_(p−1) with p = 17, so the paper would cover it if correct. That snippet is unverified. None of these is a verdict; each is a signal for the judging pass.
event.direction: Cuts in favour of the conjecture: it asserts equality (and the stronger online equality) for the two complete-graph families. Nothing in the paper cuts against it.

judgement.why: The statement is one universal equality, so no event is whole. Jafari (Aug 2026) claims equality for two infinite families of complete graphs: a case, unreviewed, and doubtful because the author is otherwise invisible, the companion manuscript is missing, and the paper was read only via a summariser; still an established-looking serious method with no identified error, so not set aside. Molloy's D+D^(2/5) bound is dated by the record only to 2024, but the first public mention is the 21 May 2024 seminar, which places it after the snapshot; it is a bound on the asymptotic error term, doubtful since no written argument exists. Vizing-type Δ+1 results (Harrelson 2022, Juvan–Mohar–Škrekovski, Vizing/ERT) bound ch′ by a different quantity and were treated as variants of the weaker Vizing conjecture rather than bounds on this one; Kahn, Molloy–Reed and Bonamy et al. bound ch′ against χ′ directly and are bounds. Single graphs (K6, K10) and the ≤10-vertex computation are instances. The AI-credited Noel and Chalise papers are on different conjectures (variants); their AI roles are recorded from their own quotes (Noel: generated; Chalise: assisted, since the model built constructions that are in the result) but do not bear on this problem. Jing's GPT-6 Pro audit is checking, hence none.
judgement.doubts: Whether 'every graph' includes multigraphs is unsettled; it does not change any scope here since all class results are cases either way. Molloy's after_snapshot rests on a seminar date taken from a search snippet. Treating Δ+1 results as variant rather than bound is a judgement call; all are pre-snapshot so it does not affect the outcome.
